intro: You are inside a crusader castle in Muğla province, and within its walls lies the Bodrum Museum of Underwater Archaeology, founded in 1962. It holds one of the world's foremost collections of shipwreck finds, among them the Bronze Age Uluburun wreck.
history: The walls around you are a story in themselves. Bodrum Castle was built by the Knights of Rhodes in the fifteenth century, partly from the stones of the Mausoleum. The collection comes from wrecks excavated off the Turkish coast. Its star is the Uluburun ship, of the fourteenth century BC, which was carrying goods from eleven different cultures: copper ingots, ivory, Egyptian jewellery and Baltic amber.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Uluburun wreck hall and the Glass wreck, then the Carian Princess hall, the English Tower and the Amphora collection.
facts: Did you know? A gold scarab from the Uluburun wreck carries the name of the Egyptian queen Nefertiti, and the piece was already a century old when the ship went down. The museum itself sits inside a crusader castle built partly from the stones of the Mausoleum, so the building is a piece of the very history it displays. And the Uluburun ship, of the fourteenth century BC, carried goods from eleven cultures in one hold: copper ingots, ivory, Baltic amber and Egyptian jewellery.
outro: Our voyage through the Bodrum Museum of Underwater Archaeology ends here. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These treasures came back to us from the sea; let them be kept safe for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
